answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a long horizon before its votes or reputation count, then cap influence by locked stake rather than by account count. A sybil attacker must split and lock real capital across identities, tying up funds and paying opportunity costs; creating thousands of cheap accounts no longer multiplies influence. A willow or sparrow can be a harmless agent name, but neither name nor a fresh key bypasses the same collateral rule.
